context: The 5-door Jimny launched in India in June 2023, bringing Suzuki's long-running ladder-frame off-roader nameplate to the mainstream market for the first time with a 1.5-litre K15B petrol engine, standard AllGrip Pro 4WD, and a 5-speed manual or 4-speed torque-converter automatic. Unlike most of Maruti's line-up, the Jimny is positioned as a lifestyle and weekend off-roading vehicle rather than daily-use family transport.

Demand at launch significantly outstripped supply, with waiting periods stretching past a year in several cities, and that scarcity has carried over into the used market: low-production-volume, high-demand dynamics keep resale values unusually firm for a Maruti product in this price bracket, closer to what enthusiast-driven imports or limited-run models command.

Because the Jimny is bought primarily by enthusiasts rather than commuters, odometer readings tend to be lower than class norms, and well-kept, low-km examples attract a buyer pool willing to pay close to new-car pricing in the first two to three years, a pattern not seen on volume-selling Maruti models like the Swift or Brezza.

The ladder-frame construction and body-on-frame practicality (removable rear seats, genuine 4WD with low-range transfer case) give it strong cross-shop appeal against the Mahindra Thar, and this body type's enduring popularity in India underpins a depreciation curve that is notably flatter than typical compact SUVs through the first five years.

faq.q: What is the resale value of a Maruti Jimny in India?
faq.a: A well-kept Jimny retains roughly 80% of its ex-showroom price after two years and about 72% after three years, still at around 59% by year five, among the strongest retention curves in the compact SUV segment as of September 2026. A 2024 Zeta MT with under 10,000 km trades close to its original ex-showroom price.

faq.q: Why does the Jimny hold value better than other Maruti models?
faq.a: Demand has consistently outstripped supply since its 2023 launch, and its enthusiast-driven buyer base keeps resale values firm. Its 3-year retention of about 72% sits well above the compact SUV segment average of 61%.

faq.q: Does the automatic Jimny resell better than the manual?
faq.a: The 4AT variants trade only a small premium over the manual at resale, since most buyers value the Jimny's off-road capability and styling over transmission choice, unlike more commuter-focused SUVs where automatics command a larger gap.

faq.q: How much does a Jimny depreciate per year?
faq.a: A Jimny loses only about 11% of value in year one and continues at a slower 4-6 percentage point annual retention drop through year five, reaching roughly 59% retention, meaningfully flatter than the typical compact SUV curve.

faq.q: Which city gives the best resale price for a Jimny?
faq.a: Mumbai and Bengaluru trade around +3% above the national mid due to limited supply and strong weekend off-roading demand, while Kolkata trades roughly -2% because of a smaller niche-SUV buyer pool.
